feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: VoiceMem: Streaming Dual-Brain Memory for Real-Time Interaction
entry.summary:
VoiceMem is a streaming dual-brain memory architecture featuring parallel informational left-brain and emotional right-brain components designed for real-time, low-latency duplex speech language models.

Why it matters: VoiceMem enables speech language models to access highly accurate factual memory and persona-driven emotional state in real time without introducing user-perceptible latency.

entry.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
entry.summary:
FrontierChallenge is a new cross-domain benchmark of 300 scientific workflows that evaluates end-to-end task completion and deliverable bundles across multiple computational sciences.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that high partial scoring and confident language model outputs do not correlate with full scientific workflow execution, requiring stricter end-to-end deliverable evaluation.

entry.title: WarpSAC: Towards the Pinnacle of Scalable Off-policy RL by Rethinking Exploration and Exploitation
entry.summary:
WarpSAC adapts off-policy RL algorithmic stabilizers based on data abundance, offering two variants that optimize exploitation and value fitting for CPU-scale and GPU-parallel training regimes.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that scaling off-policy reinforcement learning to massively parallel GPU environments requires removing data-limited constraints to achieve higher sample efficiency, faster training, and better real-world deployment performance.

entry.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
entry.summary:
JIT-Agent is a harness intelligence model that dynamically synthesizes, repairs, and evolves task-adaptive agent harnesses for off-the-shelf LLMs using a four-module composable protocol.

Why it matters: It establishes agent harness design as a trainable, automated, and transferable dimension of capability that improves model performance orthogonally to standard foundation model scaling.

entry.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed featuring 300 procedurally generated tasks and deterministic rule-based reward scorers to enable trainable, verifiable, and scalable native visual reasoning across image, video, and interleaved generators.

Why it matters: It replaces unreliable VLM-as-a-judge metrics with deterministic reward scorers, allowing models to use visual generation as an optimizable medium for complex problem solving via reinforcement learning.

entry.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
SecOPD uses on-policy distillation to provide token-level feedback for defensive fine-tuning, significantly reducing LLM vulnerability to adaptive prompt injections.

Why it matters: Token-level feedback during defensive fine-tuning effectively neutralizes adaptive prompt injections without sacrificing model performance on unseen agentic tasks.

entry.title: D^3-MOPD: Adaptive Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation
entry.summary:
D^3-MOPD dynamically schedules multi-teacher domain sampling ratios online using reverse-KL trajectories to optimize student training without adding computational overhead.

Why it matters: It enables significantly more compute-efficient multi-domain knowledge distillation by dynamically shifting training resources to slower-converging domains.

entry.title: Agent-G^2: Gaussian Guidance for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Agent-G^2 introduces a Gaussian guidance framework that dynamically samples hint depths from an online-estimated Gaussian distribution to resolve reward sparsity in agentic reinforcement learning without extra rollout costs.

Why it matters: It significantly improves task success rates in long-horizon agentic RL while cutting compute requirements by over 66% compared to probing methods.

entry.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data
entry.summary:
Mixed SFT outperforms next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data post-RLVR, achieving higher accuracy ceilings while using over 60 times less training compute.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that complex next-chunk RL is unnecessary for no-CoT data, as simple Mixed SFT provides better post-RLVR performance at a fraction of the compute cost.

entry.title: Long-Horizon Audio-Visual Generation for Persistent Stories and Interactive Worlds
entry.summary:
JoyAI-Echo-1.5 is a unified audio-visual system for generating long-horizon video narratives and interactive worlds using composable memory, geometry-aware control, and rollout-aware few-step training.

Why it matters: It enables persistent character identities, coherent audio-visual storytelling, and stable controller-agnostic camera navigation over long generation horizons.

entry.title: StreamPI: Streaming Multimodal Temporal Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models
entry.summary:
StreamPI is a parameter-free temporal modeling framework for Vision-Language-Action models that enables streaming multi-frame reasoning and asynchronous real-robot deployment.

Why it matters: It allows existing single-frame VLA models to gain temporal reasoning and real-time streaming capabilities for complex robotics tasks without requiring extra parameters.

entry.title: Video-IFBench: Evaluating Instruction Following of Multimodal LLMs in Video Understanding Scenarios
entry.summary:
Video-IFBench is a new benchmark featuring 1.5K samples across 32 task types to evaluate how well Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) follow complex user constraints in video understanding tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to measure whether video-capable MLLMs can adhere strictly to specific formatting and semantic constraints, rather than just assessing basic video content accuracy.

entry.title: Code World Model: Coding Agent as World Brain
entry.summary:
Code World Model decouples world evolution from visual generation by using a coding agent to maintain state via executable code and conditioning a video model on spatiotemporal proxy representations.

Why it matters: By relying on executable code for world state rather than purely visual priors, this architecture enables persistent consequences and rule-consistent, open-ended world simulation.

entry.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?
entry.summary:
SWE Refactor Bench evaluates coding agents on 20 whole-repository migrations across four technical debt types using a three-stage protocol that checks both migration completeness and behavioral correctness.

Why it matters: The benchmark prevents agents from cheating by copying legacy code to pass tests, exposing that current frontier models struggle with reliable, long-horizon codebase refactoring.

entry.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
V-Rubrics introduces rubric-based reinforcement learning that decomposes responses into atomic propositions to provide structured, prefix-localized reward credit across visual faithfulness, reasoning consistency, and instruction following.

Why it matters: Decomposing rewards into localized, proposition-level rubrics mitigates visual hallucination and ungrounded reasoning in vision-language models better than traditional scalar reward signals.

entry.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed with 300 procedurally generated tasks and deterministic reward scorers designed to scale, verify, and optimize native visual reasoning through image, video, and interleaved generation.

Why it matters: It establishes a verifiable, reinforcement-learning-ready framework for training multimodal models to use visual generation directly as a substrate for complex problem solving.

entry.title: Prefix Sliding for efficient test-time scaling
entry.summary:
Prefix Sliding reduces test-time scaling costs by discarding intermediate reasoning tokens while retaining the initial instruction prefix and a sliding window of recent tokens.

Why it matters: It enables models to perform ultra-long-horizon reasoning and test-time compute scaling at a fraction of the computational and memory cost.

entry.title: How Much Rank Does LoRA Need? Rank-Error Bounds for Transformer Attention
entry.summary:
This paper establishes task-dependent rank-error bounds for Query LoRA updates in Transformer attention, expressing expected KL error through the downstream-weighted tail energy of target updates.

Why it matters: It provides a theoretical foundation for selecting LoRA ranks based on task data and attention geometry rather than relying solely on trial-and-error hyperparameter tuning.

entry.title: DualOPSD: Adaptive Privileged Teachers for On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
DualOPSD introduces an asymmetric alternating framework for on-policy self-distillation that dynamically adapts the privileged teacher toward the updated student distribution without requiring extra rollouts.

Why it matters: It improves student model accuracy and generation length efficiency in self-distillation without incurring the computational overhead of generating new teacher rollouts.

entry.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
entry.summary:
AsymSpec is an asymmetric speculative decoding framework where a lightweight draft model operates on full context while a large verifier model runs on a compressed context to reduce inference costs.

Why it matters: It breaks the strict latency-accuracy trade-off in agentic LLM pipelines by preserving key reasoning signals with minimal computational overhead.

entry.title: Spectral Allocation: Why Muon Outperforms Adam, and How to Improve Muon
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Spectral-Aware Muon (SAMuon), which outperforms AdamW and Muon by using a static spectral prior to apply larger step sizes to the tolerant bulk singular directions of momentum buffers.

Why it matters: SAMuon speeds up LLM pretraining convergence by up to 24% over Muon without requiring additional persistent optimizer memory.

entry.title: SwarmWorld: Stigmergic technological evolution in societies of language-model agents
entry.summary:
SwarmWorld demonstrates that decentralized, initially homogeneous LLM agents can self-organize through environmental stigmergy and physical observation to build durable, resilient technological societies without predefined roles or direct centralized workflows.

Why it matters: It proves LLM multi-agent systems can achieve scalable collective intelligence and complex engineering through environmental modification (stigmergy) rather than relying on direct conversation or centralized control.

entry.title: $R^3$: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
$R^3$ is a post-training recipe that uses mid-training on expert traces and rubric-based RL on offline action data to train VLMs to generate free-form natural language reasoning for steering low-level robotic policies.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that free-form natural language reasoning can serve as an effective test-time compute mechanism to improve long-horizon task execution and generalization in robotic manipulation.

entry.title: ProgRouter: Online Progress-Guided Orchestration for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows under Quality-Cost Tradeoffs
entry.summary:
ProgRouter is an online routing framework that adaptively selects LLM agents step-by-step during multi-agent workflows based on task progress predictions, time constraints, and cost budgets.

Why it matters: It enables multi-agent LLM systems to solve complex tasks within strict financial and latency budgets by dynamically routing lower-cost models when full-scale models are unnecessary.

entry.title: One Symptom, Three Levers: A Critical Review of On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
This review provides a unified structural framework identifying collapse as the primary failure mode in On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) for mathematical reasoning, analyzing it through three governing levers.

Why it matters: It establishes a clear vocabulary and structural framework to help researchers analyze and prevent model collapse when using self-teacher privileged guidance instead of larger teacher models.

entry.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models
entry.summary:
EchoWM is an omnimodal world model that enables continuous camera navigation while simultaneously generating 720p video, environmental sound, speech, and music across first-person and third-person perspectives.

Why it matters: It unifies multi-modal generation with flexible 6-DoF trajectory control, enabling interactive, synchronized audio-visual media generation for virtual environments.

entry.title: Annotations as Rollouts: Efficient and Scalable Reinforcement Learning for Video MLLMs
entry.summary:
OraRL integrates ground-truth annotations as oracle rollouts during video MLLM post-training, using a decoupled advantage estimator and sign-balanced pruning to bypass slow chain-of-thought generation while improving performance.

Why it matters: It enables highly efficient RL post-training for video MLLMs, dramatically cutting decoding latency while outperforming substantially larger commercial models like GPT-5 and Gemini-3-Pro on spatial and temporal intelligence benchmarks.

entry.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report
entry.summary:
Tencent introduced WeMM-Embedding, a family of universal multimodal embedding models (2B, 4B, and 9B) supporting text, images, videos, visual documents, and interleaved multimodal inputs with flexible output dimensions.

Why it matters: WeMM-Embedding provides open-source, high-efficiency multimodal embedding models that outperform larger baselines and have proven scalable efficacy in production recommendation and search environments.

entry.title: AutoSaddler: Automatic Harness Optimization with Durable Updates from Agent Execution Traces
entry.summary:
AutoSaddler is an automatic agent harness optimization framework that treats harnesses as code and uses offline mini-batch execution traces to iteratively diagnose failures, generate patches, and select updates.

Why it matters: Automating harness design removes the manual effort required to optimize complex agent prompts, tools, and control flow for long-horizon execution tasks.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation in Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
DiffusionOPSD converts image-level reward guidance into bounded positive and negative targets for intermediate denoising predictions using an on-policy self-distillation framework with frozen behavior policies and finite fitting.

Why it matters: It improves diffusion model alignment accuracy while significantly lowering compute requirements and enabling separate analysis of target generation versus target learning.

entry.title: The Mask Is Not the Model: Auditing Prefix Invariance in Attention, State-Space, and Hybrid Sequence Models
entry.summary:
Researchers formalize prefix invariance and introduce a two-forward-pass gradient-free audit that localizes causal leaks across attention, state-space, and hybrid sequence architectures where attention-mask inspection fails.

Why it matters: Standard attention-mask checks are insufficient for ensuring causality, making empirical auditing essential for preventing future data leakage in complex or hybrid sequence models.

entry.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
entry.summary:
Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture that uses a fixed Meta-Agent to perform localized, validation-gated updates to Skill Memory based on execution evidence, preventing long-history performance degradation.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable architecture for recursive self-improvement that allows agents to handle expanding interaction horizons without getting derailed by lengthy execution histories.

entry.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) replaces action-side Policy-KL with input-side Query-KL to control query distribution shift without constraining LLM response exploration.

Why it matters: ERPO resolves the stability-exploration trade-off in LLM reinforcement learning, preventing policy drift while maintaining full action-space exploration without computational overhead.

entry.title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Practical Recipe for Recovering Compressed, 4-Bit LLMs
entry.summary:
Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) stabilizes 4-bit compressed LLM post-training by distilling directly from the original, uncompressed teacher model rather than using hard-label QAT.

Why it matters: QAH enables rapid, stable recovery of heavily compressed and 4-bit quantized LLMs without requiring multi-week hyperparameter searches.

entry.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out
entry.summary:
AutoResearch is a two-stage autonomous system that grounds research idea generation via multi-model cross-review and grounds execution using independent evidence-based review to prevent hallucinations.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that coupling grounded idea generation with rigorous automated experimental auditing significantly reduces scientific hallucinations in autonomous AI research workflows.

entry.title: From Seeing to Acting: Smart Glasses as First-Person Intelligence Platforms
entry.summary:
This survey provides a unified framework for smart glasses as first-person intelligence platforms, introducing an L0-L5 autonomy taxonomy, hardware capability axes, application scene mapping, and deployment and evaluation protocols.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized framework to design, compare, and reproducibly evaluate trustworthy egocentric AI systems operating across tightly constrained hardware and real-world deployment environments.

entry.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
entry.summary:
OPDVR combines on-policy distillation and RLVR by using a ReLU gating mechanism on trajectory correctness, eliminating extra hyperparameters while improving reasoning benchmarks.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to benefit from dense teacher distillation while ensuring policy gradient updates align strictly with verifiable task success without adding hyperparameter complexity.

entry.title: LongWoF-Bench: Evaluating EvoMap Genes for Verifiable Long-Workflow Tasks
entry.summary:
LongWoF-Bench evaluates EvoMap Genes, which externalize verifier-confirmed execution trajectories into reusable structures that significantly boost long-workflow task performance across diverse language models.

Why it matters: Consolidating verified execution trajectories into structured, reusable Genes allows models to improve long-workflow success rates and lower token costs without re-discovering strategies from scratch.

entry.title: Better Retrieval, Worse Robustness:How Multi-hop RAG Amplifies Upstream ASR Errors
entry.summary:
Multi-hop RAG extensions like entity-graph linking and iterative reformulation amplify upstream ASR errors, resulting in a 36-67% larger clean-to-noisy F1 performance gap than naive dense retrieval across three benchmarks.

Why it matters: Building voice-driven multi-hop RAG systems requires addressing structural error amplification, as standard graph and iterative retrieval techniques degrade significantly when exposed to noisy ASR inputs.

entry.title: Industrial-Instruction: An End-to-End Framework for Building Instruction-Tuning and Benchmark Datasets from Industrial Technical Reports
entry.summary:
Industrial-Instruction introduces an end-to-end pipeline and two open QA datasets derived from Panasonic technical reports to benchmark and fine-tune LLMs on industrial troubleshooting, maintenance, and specification data.

Why it matters: It provides a reproducible framework to transform complex, multi-modal industrial technical documentation into effective instruction-tuning data and benchmarks for targeted enterprise LLM deployment.

entry.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses
entry.summary:
Recuris introduces a recursive Experiential-Working Memory architecture that decouples long-horizon state tracking from skill execution, using a fixed Meta-Agent to perform localized, validation-gated memory updates.

Why it matters: It establishes localized, memory-level updates as a scalable mechanism for recursive self-improvement in LLM agents without needing full context history or model re-training.

entry.title: SPO++: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL
entry.summary:
SPO++ enhances asynchronous agentic RL by standardizing terminal-outcome advantages under the action-token measure and organizing prompt evidence by policy event generation order rather than learner receipt order.

Why it matters: It eliminates training delays in variable-length, tool-use RL trajectories without sacrificing policy optimization stability or sample efficiency.

entry.title: CAFE: Self-Improving Search Agents Need Co-Evolving Feedback
entry.summary:
CAFE is a framework where a shared-parameter model alternates between search-agent and critic roles to co-evolve corrective feedback alongside policy updates.

Why it matters: Co-evolving in-trajectory feedback prevents optimization plateaus in self-improving search agents and leads to lower hallucination rates during complex retrievals.

entry.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
entry.summary:
Meta$^n$ achieves recursive self-improvement beyond two meta-levels by holding a meta-operation fixed and repeatedly applying it to its own traces and code to generate subsequent layers.

Why it matters: It bypasses the traditional stability-driven caps on meta-depth in LLM agents, enabling continuous strategic self-improvement without destabilizing editing machinery.

entry.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
entry.summary:
OPDVR combines on-policy distillation and verifiable reward RL by reformulating sampled-token OPD implicit rewards with trajectory correctness and a ReLU gating mechanism, eliminating extra hyperparameters while outperforming standard OPD across six reasoning benchmarks.

Why it matters: It aligns dense token-level teacher guidance with task-level correctness without adding hyperparameter tuning overhead or performance trade-offs.

entry.title: The Invisible Editorial Layer: Formalizing Undisclosed Inference-Time Steering, Probability Placement, and the Attribution Problem in Deployed Language Models
entry.summary:
This paper formalizes undisclosed inference-time steering—systematic logit-level modifications applied before token sampling—and introduces frameworks for attributing behavioral bias, modeling probability placement advertising, and establishing inference policy transparency.

Why it matters: It highlights how undisclosed post-inference logit modifications can secretly manipulate political or commercial framing in LLM outputs, complicating regulatory oversight and bias attribution.

entry.title: Parason: Revealing Subtask and Trial Parallelism in LLM Reasoning
entry.summary:
Parason introduces a framework to learn and execute both subtask and trial parallelism in LLM reasoning traces, accelerating inference on complex math benchmarks using Parallelism-Aware GRPO.

Why it matters: By unlocking trial parallelism alongside subtask parallelism, Parason significantly reduces inference latency for long test-time LLM reasoning traces without sacrificing problem-solving accuracy.

entry.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
entry.summary:
Language model pretraining loss dynamics collapse onto a single trajectory when runs match their effective learning rate (ELR), defined as the ratio of learning rate to parameter norm.

Why it matters: ELR serves as a unified coordinate that links learning rate scheduling, norm-control interventions, and scaling laws to simplify pretraining optimization.

entry.title: WeMM-Embedding: WeChat Multi-Modal Embedding Technical Report
entry.summary:
Tencent has released WeMM-Embedding, a family of 2B, 4B, and 9B universal multimodal embedding models supporting text, images, videos, visual documents, and interleaved inputs with flexible output dimensions.

Why it matters: It offers open-source, production-proven multimodal embedding models that outperform larger existing baselines in retrieval, search, and recommendation tasks.

entry.title: Curved Inference II: Sleeper Agent Geometry - Extending Interpretability Beyond Probes
entry.summary:
Curved Inference II introduces semantic surface area (A'), an unsupervised geometric metric in unnormalised residual space that detects naturalistic deceptive reasoning without reliance on backdoors, artificial triggers, or linear probes.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable, unsupervised detection method for deceptive alignment based on the intrinsic geometric shape of inference, even when models suppress linear indicators.

entry.title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work
entry.summary:
Apodex 1.1 introduces environment and agentic coordination scaling to handle long-horizon, verifiable tasks, achieving top-tier performance at smaller model scales.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that long-running, complex professional work can be automated effectively using smaller, locally deployable models combined with robust execution infrastructure.

entry.title: MobilePA-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Planner Agents on Complex Real-World Tasks
entry.summary:
MobilePA-Bench is an interactive, stateful benchmark for evaluating mobile planning agents using an executable sandbox across 13 domains and 212 tools.

Why it matters: It provides a realistic runtime environment to test and train mobile agents on complex long-horizon planning, sub-agent delegation, and error recovery.

entry.title: RISE: Adaptive Imagination for World Action Models
entry.summary:
RISE introduces an adaptive imagination framework that uses a Latent Evaluator and Rollout Gate to dynamically make sequential Roll/Stop decisions for World Action Models based on expected planning benefits versus compute costs.

Why it matters: It enables World Action Models to achieve optimal safety and planning accuracy in autonomous driving while significantly cutting inference-time computation through dynamic imagination budgets.

entry.title: TLive-Omni: An Omni-Modal Understanding Model for E-Commerce Live Streaming
entry.summary:
TLive-Omni is an omni-modal model for e-commerce live streaming that unifies video, audio, image, and text inputs using a timestamped Per-vGrid temporal token organization.

Why it matters: It enables accurate, real-time omni-modal understanding of complex, noisy, long-form live-commerce streams across multiple parallel input modalities.

entry.title: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
entry.summary:
Prime Agent is an open-source harness for long-horizon agent workflows using a persistent IPython REPL and a Continual Harness system that preserves execution history and subagent state across trajectories.

Why it matters: By standardizing execution, recovery, and verification, Prime Agent minimizes harness-level failures to measure and unlock an LM's maximal long-horizon problem-solving capabilities.

entry.title: Block3D: Efficient Text-to-3D Generation via Block-Wise Diffusion
entry.summary:
Block3D introduces a block-wise diffusion framework for text-to-3D generation that combines autoregressive block generation with joint token denoising to achieve a 5.15x speedup.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the latency and compute cost of high-fidelity text-to-3D generation by combining the strengths of autoregressive models and diffusion processes.

entry.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
entry.summary:
ReWorld is an interactive world model that combines mixed per-head attention windows, pose-indexed landmark retrieval, and metric-aligned data to achieve long-horizon memory and high control fidelity in real-time video streaming.

Why it matters: It enables real-time interactive video generation and simulation over extended timeframes without memory overflow or loss of long-term spatial consistency.

entry.title: Partition the Support, Reconstruct the Residual: Training-Free Sparse Attention for Video Generation and World Models
entry.summary:
SparsePR is a training-free sparse attention method that uses Response-Coupled Partitioning and Probe-Fitted Residual Reconstruction to accelerate video transformers while minimizing post-softmax reconstruction error.

Why it matters: SparsePR enables significant end-to-end execution speedups for video generation and world models without retraining or sacrificing output quality.

entry.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control
entry.summary:
Hydra-0 is a generalist world model that represents robot actions as pixel-level action flow, enabling cross-embodiment learning, open-loop policy evaluation, and action generation from human demonstrations.

Why it matters: By unifying heterogeneous visual data through pixel motion, Hydra-0 allows robots to learn control and evaluate policies directly from human demonstrations without needing expert robot training data.

entry.title: GameXpert-Bench: How Far Are Coding Agents from Expert Game Development?
entry.summary:
GameXpert-Bench evaluates LLM coding agents across three game development lifecycle stages: complete game generation, bug diagnosis and repair, and multi-turn request optimization.

Why it matters: It provides a holistic, lifecycle-based benchmark to identify where autonomous LLM coding agents fail when building complex, interactive multi-modal applications.

entry.title: One Success Isn't Reliability: Thinkingbox, a Sandbox and Benchmark for Agents in Stateful Business Workflows
entry.summary:
Microsoft introduced Thinkingbox and Thinkingbox-bench, an execution sandbox and 507-workflow benchmark evaluating AI agents on stateful business tasks using MCP-compatible tool sessions and backend state checks.

Why it matters: High pass@1 scores mask agent unreliability, showing that current models struggle with consistent, error-free execution in stateful enterprise workflows.

entry.title: Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress
entry.summary:
R2-OPD improves on-policy distillation by using progress rewards to filter out teacher supervision that conflicts with actual reasoning progress.

Why it matters: It prevents models from penalizing correct reasoning paths during distillation simply because they diverge from the teacher's exact output generation.

entry.title: Task-CoEvolve: Efficient Harness Optimization via Adaptive Validation Task Selection
entry.summary:
Task-CoEvolve optimizes LLM harnesses by adaptively co-evolving validation tasks using variance-weighted sampling and probability-adjusted score estimation, reducing evaluation costs by 80% while matching full-set optimization performance.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs for prompt and code harness optimization without compromising final model performance on complex benchmarks.

entry.title: PhysCaP: Grounding Code-as-Policy Agent with Physics-Informed Exploration
entry.summary:
PhysCaP introduces a training-free, dual-agent Code-as-Policy framework that uses physics-informed active exploration to estimate latent physical properties like mass and stiffness from proprioception.

Why it matters: It enables vision-language-action policies to manipulate objects with hidden or non-visual physical attributes using targeted, low-cost physical exploration.

entry.title: Peer-Voted LLM-Agent Stress Tests Find Feed-Induced Lexical Convergence but No Reliable Matched-Exposure Advantage for Distributed Sources
entry.summary:
Researchers developed PV-SST, a peer-voted social-platform testbed, finding that peer-ranked feeds induce lexical convergence in LLM-agent populations but do not provide a reliable opinion-shifting advantage for distributed sources.

Why it matters: The findings demonstrate that while peer-ranked feeds reliably homogenize the vocabulary of LLM-agent populations, they do not inherently drive reliable opinion capture or coordination advantages.

entry.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
entry.summary:
Best-Practice Critic Optimization (BPCO) stabilizes critic-based RL for LLMs, enabling single-response advantage estimation that matches or exceeds group-based methods like GRPO.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs during RL training by requiring only one response per prompt while maintaining or improving model performance over multi-sample baselines.

entry.title: ConvergeFlow: Language Flow with Provable Convergence to Token Embeddings
entry.summary:
ConvergeFlow is an embedding-space flow-based language model that constrains data prediction to the convex hull of token embeddings, guaranteeing mathematical convergence to valid embeddings without needing a cross-entropy-supervised decoder.

Why it matters: It establishes a theoretical foundation for continuous flow LMs by enabling direct token prediction via flow convergence, simplifying model architectures by removing the cross-entropy decoder.

entry.title: Mitigating Reasoning-Induced Misalignment via Safety-Direction Penalty
entry.summary:
Researchers identified safety-reasoning representation coupling in LLMs and introduced Safety-Direction Penalty (SDP), a training-time loss that penalizes movement along learned safety directions to prevent reasoning-induced misalignment.

Why it matters: SDP provides a targeted geometric fix during fine-tuning to prevent reasoning data from inadvertently weakening model safety guardrails.

entry.title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
entry.summary:
Self-Reflective Policy Optimization (SRPO) converts sparse terminal rewards into dense token-level training signals by having LLMs generate self-reflection patches to score student on-policy rollouts without external critics or larger teacher models.

Why it matters: SRPO provides a highly FLOP-efficient post-training method that enables LLMs to improve long-horizon reasoning and agentic task performance without reliance on external reward modeling infrastructure.

entry.title: Is Next-Chunk Reasoning RL Really Better than SFT? Revisiting Training Strategies under no-CoT Data
entry.summary:
Mixed SFT outperforms next-chunk reasoning RL on no-CoT data post-RLVR, achieving higher accuracy ceilings with over 60 times less compute.

Why it matters: Simple single-stage SFT provides a far more compute-efficient base than next-chunk RL for maximizing final model performance after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards.

entry.title: Credal Large Language Models for Semantic Commitment under Uncertainty
entry.summary:
Credal Large Language Models (CLLMs) use LoRA ensembles to capture uncertainty via lower and upper probabilities, enabling token and semantic commitment scores for improved calibration and hallucination detection.

Why it matters: CLLMs disentangle epistemic ignorance from ambiguity, enabling more reliable hallucination detection and selective prediction in safety-critical LLM deployments.

entry.title: ProxyFormer: A Dual-Stream Proxy Architecture for Ultra-Long Context and High-Resolution Generation
entry.summary:
ProxyFormer is a dual-stream architecture that compresses local features into proxy tokens for global attention, extending trainable sequence lengths to ~0.7M tokens on a 16GB GPU at a 64x compression ratio.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces attention memory and compute requirements, enabling ultra-long-context training and high-resolution generation on consumer-grade hardware.

entry.title: A Physical Response-and-Memory Model for Muon Optimization
entry.summary:
A physical response-and-memory model of weight matrices explains Muon's success and introduces Bi-Maxwell, a dual-timescale optimizer that reaches target LLM losses in fewer steps.

Why it matters: Grounding optimizer design in a physical framework allows for principled memory kernel tuning, accelerating LLM convergence and reducing compute costs.

entry.title: Beyond the Stability-Exploration Dilemma: Environmental Regularization for LLM Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
Environment-Regularized Policy Optimization (ERPO) replaces the standard action-side Policy-KL regularizer with a input-side Query-KL (QKL) term to prevent query distribution drift while preserving response-level exploration in LLMs.

Why it matters: ERPO eliminates the trade-off between policy stability and response-level exploration, enabling safer, long-horizon LLM reinforcement learning without extra computational overhead.

entry.title: Accelerating Diffusion Language Models via Structured Suffix Modeling
entry.summary:
Structured Suffix Modeling accelerates Diffusion Language Model inference training-free by splitting the token suffix into three distinct structural regions and reusing previous-step decoding representations.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the computational overhead of parallel decoding in Diffusion Language Models while preserving or improving generation performance without needing model retraining.

entry.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
entry.summary:
OmniAssistBench is a new benchmark for evaluating omni-modal LLMs as real-time video assistants using multi-turn video clips reverse-engineered from Internet videos.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized methodology to evaluate real-time, interactive omni-modal models on active dynamic guidance tasks rather than passive video understanding.

entry.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts
entry.summary:
A two-step framework transfers optimal learning rates across model widths and extrapolates them to trillion-token training horizons using proxy models.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need for expensive hyperparameter sweeps when training large-scale MoE models over massive token budgets.

entry.title: Graph Engineering in the Era of LLM Agents: From Individual Intelligence to System Intelligence
entry.summary:
Graph Engineering introduces explicit, dynamic graph structures representing tasks, agents, and system states to advance multi-agent LLM systems from individual to system intelligence.

Why it matters: It provides an architectural framework to scale AI systems beyond single-agent limits by using dynamic graphs to orchestrate specialized, interdependent agents.

entry.title: EviRank: Structured Relevance Evidence for Multimodal Image Re-ranking
entry.summary:
EviRank introduces a training-free framework that parses multimodal search queries into structured, six-slot evidence packages for transparent, constraint-based image re-ranking.

Why it matters: It eliminates opaque embeddings and hallucinatory chain-of-thought outputs by recasting multimodal image re-ranking as verifiable, fine-grained semantic constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: InfinityEdit: Infinite Video Editing with a Lightweight Edit-Ignition Adapter
entry.summary:
InfinityEdit introduces a lightweight edit-ignition adapter that enables streaming video generators to process unbounded, sequential edit instructions on open-ended video streams without relying on fixed-length, frame-by-frame static inputs.

Why it matters: It allows real-time, continuous video editing for open-ended streams—such as live game restyling—without quality degradation as edits accumulate over time.

entry.title: AgentMercury: Your Agent Can Synthesize Verifiable Environments for Business Scenarios at scale
entry.summary:
AgentMercury synthesizes verifiable, executable business environments at scale to train AI agents via reinforcement learning using scenario-grounded world models instead of predefined task benchmarks.

Why it matters: Training agents on auto-generated business environments improves generalizability across enterprise workflows, reasoning, coding, and tool-use tasks without relying on target-specific benchmarks.

entry.title: Towards Faithful Simulation of Human Shopping Behavior
entry.summary:
RecVerse is a GUI-grounded user simulation agent that uses a cognitive hierarchical memory and a trajectory-level RL objective to produce realistic multi-turn e-commerce shopping sessions.

Why it matters: It improves the fidelity of offline evaluation and reinforcement learning environments for e-commerce recommendation systems by mitigating common simulation errors like over-exploration and passivity.

entry.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
entry.summary:
CLEAR uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously scale a safety LoRA adapter's activation, preserving base LLM utility while reducing harmful responses.

Why it matters: It offers a conditional routing approach to safety alignment that maintains model robustness against harmful prompts without compromising performance on general reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs
entry.summary:
Llama-Mobile introduces a quantization framework that uses self-generated training data to compress Vision-Language Models into a novel 2.7-bit-per-parameter format optimized for Arm CPUs.

Why it matters: It enables the deployment of large 11B parameter Vision-Language Models directly on resource-constrained mobile hardware with Arm CPUs.

entry.title: Daedalus-150M: A Convolution-Attention Hybrid Designed for CPU Inference
entry.summary:
Daedalus-150M is a 150M-parameter convolution-attention hybrid LLM designed specifically for CPU inference that outperforms larger baseline models while decoding up to 2.08x faster at a 2048-token context length.

Why it matters: By restricting attention to a fraction of layers, hybrid architectures can drastically reduce the memory and compute overhead of long context lengths on standard CPUs.

entry.title: From Attention Masks to Inert Zero-Vector Tokens: OAttention and O-Closure for Token Dynamics
entry.summary:
OAttention introduces an active-presence coefficient based on hidden-carrier norm that turns zero-vector tokens into non-participating inert elements while establishing compositional O-Closure across transformer blocks.

Why it matters: It enables mathematically exact null-token dynamics and inert zero-vector insertions without altering standard attention scoring or requiring retraining from scratch.

entry.title: Don't Solve, Just Compare: Tiny Advisors for Runtime Intervention in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Comparison-Only Tiny Advisor (COTA) improves LLM agent reliability by using a small model to compare candidate continuations and supply non-binding advice without needing full task-solving capabilities.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that runtime intervention can enhance LLM agent performance using lightweight auxiliary models that possess significantly less task-solving capacity than the primary actor.

entry.title: Jacobian-guided Noise Injection for Quantization Robustness in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
A training strategy injects zero-mean Gaussian noise into pre-attention logits using variance derived from the softmax Jacobian Frobenius norm to improve LLM post-training quantization robustness.

Why it matters: It enables lower-bit quantization of vision and language transformers with significantly less performance degradation by stabilizing the self-attention mechanism during training.

entry.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training
entry.summary:
E$^2$-TTT uses a derived closed-form state transition to achieve parallelized chunk-wise training that exactly matches the per-token fast-weight and momentum updates of Test-Time Training.

Why it matters: It eliminates the tradeoff between per-token expressivity and chunk-wise hardware efficiency in Test-Time Training architectures.

entry.title: Nothing Changed but the Model: CellFill -- Bounded In-Cell Learning for Bit-Identical, Revocable Updates to Quantized LLMs
entry.summary:
CellFill achieves bit-identical, revocable LLM updates by training bounded per-weight residuals strictly within the dequantization gap of frozen 4-bit quantization cells.

Why it matters: It allows deployed quantized models to incorporate new knowledge without invalidating prior evaluations, breaking KV caches, or altering base model checkpoints.

entry.title: SAC-Copula: Quality-Preserving Watermarking for Diffusion Language Models via Smooth Correlated Gumbel Fields
entry.summary:
SAC-Copula introduces smooth, locally correlated Gumbel perturbation fields via a Gaussian copula to watermark diffusion language models without degrading generation quality.

Why it matters: It enables reliable detection of text generated by diffusion language models while preserving generation quality and stability during iterative refinement.

entry.title: Memory Augmentation Unlocks Efficient Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
entry.summary:
A training-free framework called Memory-Augmented Compression retrieves historical reasoning patterns to prefill context, enabling compressed Chain-of-Thought reasoning without sacrificing accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to perform complex reasoning tasks significantly faster and with lower decode-time overhead while improving accuracy over existing compression methods.

entry.title: RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
entry.summary:
RARE enables effective representation steering in MoE language models by projecting behavioral perturbations onto the router matrix's null space to maintain expert routing consistency.

Why it matters: It allows lightweight inference-time control of MoE models without causing performance degradation from broken expert routing.

entry.title: Sparse Token Routing in Efficient Transformers
entry.summary:
Evaluating the SEWN two-stream Transformer shows that learned sparse token routing yields negligible accuracy gains over parameter-matched baselines, though contextual gates produce robust token-importance signals.

Why it matters: The findings challenge the assumption that dynamic token routing improves Transformer performance efficiency over simpler parameter-matched baselines.

entry.title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation
entry.summary:
Researchers developed the Open-Weight Masked Introspection framework to test model self-auditing across eight open-weight models, finding zero intrinsic ability to verbally report internal computational interventions.

Why it matters: Safety oversight mechanisms cannot rely on a model's untuned verbal self-reports to detect internal state changes or tampering, requiring internal probing or explicit calibration instead.

entry.title: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary:
LiLiCorr improves speculative decoding draft coherence by using lightweight in/out vector cosine similarity across top-k candidates to select jointly coherent token blocks.

Why it matters: It enables significantly higher inference throughput for speculative decoding with diffusion-style drafters at a negligible latency cost of under 3%.

entry.title: Re$^3$Cap: Retrieval-Guided Refinement for Image Captioning Enhancement via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Re3Cap introduces a retrieval-guided reasoning strategy that uses multi-modal retrieval to guide reinforcement learning for image captioning without additional annotations.

Why it matters: It enables Large Vision-Language Models to generate more detailed and accurate captions via reinforcement learning without relying on additional human annotations.

entry.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
entry.summary:
CLEAR introduces a conditional safety adaptation framework that uses a lightweight hidden-state gate to continuously scale the activation strength of a safety LoRA adapter, optimizing the safety-utility trade-off.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that dynamic, input-conditional adapter routing can preserve model performance on benign tasks while effectively mitigating harmful completions.

entry.title: Utility Under Attack: Agent Memory Poisoning and the Limits of Content Screening and Provenance Ranking
entry.summary:
A study demonstrates that unoptimized false assertions in 1.2% of a agent memory corpus reduce retrieval accuracy from 0.850 to 0.300, while bypassing content screening and breaking additive provenance ranking.

Why it matters: Simple memory poisoning attacks easily bypass standard safety guardrails and reveal fundamental flaws in relying on additive provenance weights to secure persistent LLM memory.

entry.title: Personalized Privacy Control in LLMs via Attention Head Intervention
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce personalized privacy for LLMs, evaluate prompt failures via P3Bench, and propose REPAIR, an inference-time attention head intervention method to enforce user-specific disclosure preferences.

Why it matters: System prompts alone are insufficient to prevent LLM agents from leaking sensitive user data, making internal mechanistic interventions like REPAIR necessary for reliable privacy enforcement.
